skill.name: frontend-api-client-with-jwt
skill.description: Guides the design of a centralized Next.js API client that handles JWT authorization, token refresh, and error responses.
skill.summary: Design a JWT-aware API client for Next.js applications.
skill.author: Claude

security_audit.summary: All six static findings are false positives caused by ordinary JWT API-client terminology such as token, Unauthorized, context, and blocking. The skill contains conceptual Next.js authentication guidance and security best practices, with no code, network targets, exfiltration instructions, prompt injection, or reconnaissance intent.

static_findings.snippet: 4. **Error Information**: Avoid exposing sensitive information in error messages
- Implement efficient token refresh to avoid blocking requests

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 74 lists a valid JWT token as required input for authorization in a legitimate API client. It does not instruct the agent to inspect the host system or gather system data.
Line 100 describes the HTTP 401 Unauthorized response for expired or invalid JWTs. This is normal error-handling documentation, not system reconnaissance.
Line 141 advises avoiding sensitive information in error messages. This is defensive security guidance and does not request disclosure or collection of sensitive system information.
Line 149 discusses avoiding request delays during token refresh. The word blocking refers to frontend request performance, not access control bypass or system inspection.
Line 166 recommends testing token attachment with valid and invalid tokens. This is standard authentication test coverage and does not direct reconnaissance against a system.
Line 132 refers to React context-based API client access. It does not ask the agent to discover network hosts, enumerate endpoints, or probe external services.

content.user_title: Build JWT API Clients for Next.js
content.value_statement: Frontend apps often duplicate token handling and error parsing. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to design one JWT-aware API client.
actual_capabilities: Defines responsibilities for a centralized Next.js API communication layer.
Guides Authorization header attachment with Bearer JWT tokens.
Explains token expiration checks, refresh flows, and refresh failure handling.
Outlines parsing for 401, 403, network, client, and server errors.
Covers client-side, server-side, and React component integration patterns.
Lists security, performance, validation, and testing considerations.
limitations: It is conceptual guidance and does not include ready-to-run source files.
It assumes JWT-based authentication and is less useful for other auth models.
It does not choose a specific storage strategy for every threat model.
It requires project-specific endpoint, routing, and state management details.

use_cases.title: Create a Shared API Layer
use_cases.description: Plan a reusable client that standardizes requests, responses, errors, and authentication behavior.

use_cases.title: Review Authentication Architecture
use_cases.description: Check whether a Next.js app handles token refresh, redirects, and server/client boundaries consistently.

use_cases.title: Design Auth Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Identify test scenarios for valid tokens, expired tokens, refresh failures, concurrent requests, and error responses.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Next.js app
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a simple centralized API client for my Next.js app. Include JWT header attachment, base URL handling, and basic error responses.

prompt_templates.title: Add Token Refresh
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend my API client design with JWT expiration checks, token refresh, retry behavior, and redirect handling when refresh fails.

prompt_templates.title: Support React Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to expose the API client through React hooks or context while keeping token handling consistent across components.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Next.js JWT API client for security, performance, concurrency, error handling, and test coverage gaps.

output_examples.input: Design a JWT-aware client for a Next.js dashboard.
output: A shared client should own base URL handling, Authorization headers, timeouts, and response parsing.
Token refresh should run once for concurrent requests, then retry eligible requests after a successful refresh.
Authentication failures should clear session state and route users to the login flow.

output_examples.input: Review token refresh behavior for reliability.
output: Check token expiration before requests and treat 401 responses as a possible refresh trigger.
Prevent multiple simultaneous refresh calls when many requests fail together.
Test refresh failure, invalid token, network timeout, and permission-denied scenarios.

output_examples.input: List security considerations for frontend token handling.
output: Use HTTPS for every authenticated request and avoid logging token values.
Choose storage based on XSS, CSRF, and server-rendering requirements.
Return user-safe error messages while keeping sensitive diagnostics out of the UI.

best_practices: Keep token attachment, refresh, and error parsing in one shared client layer.
Model client-side and server-side execution contexts before choosing token storage.
Test expiration, refresh failure, concurrent requests, and authorization errors.
anti_patterns: Do not duplicate Authorization header logic across many components.
Do not expose raw token values or sensitive server details in logs or UI errors.
Do not retry every failed request without checking status, method, and refresh state.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete API client?
faq.answer: It provides implementation guidance and architecture prompts, but it does not ship a complete source package.

faq.question: Can it be used with the Next.js App Router?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers both client-side and server-side contexts that are relevant to App Router projects.

faq.question: Does it require JWT authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is designed for JWT-based access tokens and refresh flows.

faq.question: Can it help choose token storage?
faq.answer: It can compare options such as cookies and browser storage, but the final choice depends on your threat model.

faq.question: Does it cover error handling?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines handling for authentication errors, authorization errors, general HTTP errors, and network failures.

faq.question: Is it useful for testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists test areas for token attachment, refresh behavior, invalid tokens, and concurrent request handling.
